options: A named notification target, typically an email address or distribution list
questions.explain: An operator is who gets told when an alert fires — created with sp_add_operator and an @email_address.

questions.q: Which severity range does SQL Server treat as fatal errors, and the range a DBA typically alerts on?
questions.explain: Severities 19 through 25 represent fatal errors — the range worth building alerts and notifications around.

questions.q: In sp_add_alert, what does setting @message_id = 0 alongside a @severity value mean?
options: Fire on any error that occurs at that severity level, not one specific numbered error
Disable the alert until a message_id is assigned
Fire only when message_id is exactly zero, which never happens
questions.explain: @message_id = 0 combined with a @severity makes the alert match any error at that severity, rather than a single specific error number.

questions.q: An alert exists and an operator exists with a valid email, but nobody gets notified when it fires. What's most likely missing?
options: sp_add_notification was never run to link the alert to the operator
The operator's email address must be re-entered every time an alert fires
Alerts cannot notify operators — only jobs can
The SQL Server Agent service needs SMTP credentials hardcoded
questions.explain: Creating an alert and an operator independently doesn't connect them — sp_add_notification is the step that wires the two together.

questions.explain: @notification_method selects how the operator is contacted; 1 corresponds to email.
